records.description: Run each SLSQP restart for only PROBE_ITER=50 iterations, and continue to MAX_ITER only those whose probe radius sum is at or above the 75th percentile of probes seen so far, so more of the time budget goes to promising basins.
In the second half of the time budget, half of the SLSQP restarts start from the best centres found so far with Gaussian jitter (sd 0.03), and the rest stay uniform random.
Seed half of the non-guided SLSQP restarts from a randomly rotated, scaled hexagonal lattice of 32 points centred in the square (with the usual 0.03 noise), instead of uniform sampling.

Guided restarts in the second half of the budget use a crossover of the best and previous-best packings (left part of one, right part of the other along a random vertical or horizontal cut, count fixed to n) as the SLSQP start instead of the best packing alone.

Replace the first SLSQP stage with an analytic-gradient quadratic penalty on overlaps and boundary violations, minimised by L-BFGS-B while the penalty weight rises from 10 to 1e5, then polish with the existing SLSQP.
Give SLSQP analytic gradients for the objective and for the full constraint vector (pair distances, boundary terms, radii), so each restart runs faster and more restarts fit in the time budget.

Replace the uniform random initial centres of the non-guided SLSQP restarts with a jittered 6x6 grid (32 of 36 lattice points chosen at random, plus small uniform jitter), leaving guided restarts unchanged.

Basin-hopping perturbation of the best packing, as specified, is already what the incumbent's guided restarts do (Gaussian jitter of sd 0.03 on the best centres, re-run SLSQP, keep only if the radius sum improves), so this idea would not add a new change.
Switch to local perturbation of the best packing after 40% of the time budget (instead of 50%), with every later restart perturbing the best instead of a coin flip at 50%.

After each repair, greedily grow every circle's radius (random order from the seed rng) to the largest value allowed by the walls and its neighbours, repeating until no radius grows by more than 1e-12, to recover radius lost to the conservative repair.
With probability 0.5 per restart (even n only), first solve a 180-degree point-symmetric half-size SLSQP problem, then start a full unconstrained SLSQP run from its output.

Add a gravity pull term lam * sum_i ||c_i - (0.5, 0.5)||^2 to each SLSQP restart's objective, with lam starting at 0.05 and decaying linearly to zero over the iterations (updated via the SLSQP callback), so the final objective is the true sum of radii.
Restrict SLSQP's pairwise non-overlap constraints to pairs whose starting centres are within 0.25 (about 2.5 times the typical final radius), so each restart uses fewer constraints and runs faster.
Over-provision each restart by solving for n+2 circles, drop the two smallest after repair, re-optimise the remaining n with a second SLSQP, and keep the best-of-restarts logic unchanged.

Anneal a random clearance margin delta (0.01 to 0.03) to zero over three sequential SLSQP stages inside _solve_once, so intermediate packings keep clearance and the final unconstrained stage moves less.

issues: No sign of gaming the measurement. There is no file or network access, no pasted coordinates and no use of labels. All randomness comes from the seeded rng, and the existing _repair step still runs on every candidate, so the packings stay valid.

No bug makes the result meaningless. _destroy copies c and r before changing them. If the disc contains no centres, idx is empty and the start is simply left as it was. Re-placed centres are clipped to [0,1] and given radius 0.01, which is a sensible start for SLSQP. The call _destroy(*best, rng) only works if best has exactly two items (c, r). The job finished with a score, so it does.

Behaviour change to note: guided restarts used to be the incumbent's best centres plus Gaussian noise (sd 0.03) with radii reset to INIT_RADIUS. Now they keep the best radii and re-place only the circles inside a random disc. This is a real change to the search method, not a bug.

The numbers support the reported z. The candidate's sum of radii is 0.0058 lower (2.9307 vs 2.9365). With noise sd 0.0034 and one run on each side, z = -0.0058 / (0.0034 * sqrt(2)) = -1.21. The harness value of -1.187 fits once the 4-decimal rounding of the inputs is allowed for (the range is about -1.19 to -1.23).

The evidence is weak: one run against one run, |z| about 1.2. The candidate looks somewhat worse, but this is not conclusive. Rejecting is reasonable, and no replicate is needed unless large-neighbourhood search is a priority idea.

records.description: After the first half of the budget, the guided restarts replace the global jitter of the incumbent with a destroy-and-repair move: a random disc (centre uniform in the square, radius uniform in [0.2, 0.4]) has its circles re-placed uniformly inside it with radius 0.01, then SLSQP runs on all circles and the existing keep-if-better check applies.

Seed each guided restart from the best 31-circle packing (found in the first 15% of the budget) plus one circle inserted at the grid point with the most clearance, with radius 0.01, instead of from the best 32-circle packing.

After the random-restart phase, polish the top K=3 distinct repaired packings each with one SLSQP run (MAX_ITER 1000, ftol 1e-12) started from its own configuration, repair the results, and return the packing with the largest sum of radii.

Add a radius-continuation restart: with probability 0.5 per non-guided restart, bisect a common radius rho in [0.05, 0.2] (6 steps, SLSQP maximising the minimum clearance) and start the sum-of-radii SLSQP from the feasible centres with radii set to rho.

Replace the uniform random initial centres of the non-guided restarts with blocks of a scrambled Halton sequence (bases 2 and 3, digit permutations and start index drawn from the seed rng, mapped to [0.05, 0.95]^2), so successive restarts cover the square more evenly; radii init and the rest of the loop are unchanged.

Replace the random restarts with successive halving: pools of 16 random starts run SLSQP in rounds of doubling iteration budgets (40, 80, 160, 320), keeping the top half by repaired radius sum each round, and the best packing across all pools is returned; this replaces the guided restarts of the incumbent.

Replace the guided-restart logic with a population of the best 8 repaired packings: each new SLSQP start perturbs a randomly chosen member, and the result replaces the worst member if its radius sum is higher.

Before the free-radius SLSQP stage, first maximise the minimum pairwise slack of the centres with all radii fixed equal (SLSQP with a slack variable t), then start the free stage from those centres so the sum-of-radii optimisation begins from a well-spread layout.

issues: Integrity: no file or network access, no pasted coordinates, and no use of test labels. The new _lsg_init draws all its randomness from the seeded rng, and the result still goes through SLSQP and the existing repair step, so the validity check is not bypassed.

Bugs: none that make the result meaningless. Adding eye to dist avoids division by zero on the diagonal, and the (n,2) boolean mask on v is valid. Radii from _lsg_init can end up slightly larger than the wall gap or slightly overlapping after the push step. That is harmless because they are only a starting point for SLSQP and the repair step.
Side effect: the extra rng.random() call shifts the random stream compared with the incumbent. This is not a problem, but it means per-seed results cannot be compared one to one.
Cost: 300 steps of O(n^2) work with n=32 is cheap, so there is no meaningful risk of going over the time limit.

Numbers: candidate -2.9365 vs incumbent -2.9365, one run each. The difference is 0, so z = 0/(0.0034*sqrt(2)) = 0, which matches the harness. The reject decision is consistent because there is no evidence of a gain, and the change adds about 20 lines of code.
The incumbent mean comes from a single run and is already close to the best published value of about 2.9370, so there is little room left to show a gain at this noise level.

records.description: Add a Lubachevsky-Stillinger style soft-disk growth initialiser (300 steps, seeded velocities) used for about a third of non-guided SLSQP restarts, with its centres and radii passed to SLSQP as the start.

Replace the independent restarts with a single Metropolis chain: each step re-initialises 3 to 5 random circles, re-optimises with SLSQP, repairs, and accepts worse packings with probability exp(delta/T), where T decays geometrically from 0.01 to 0.0001 over the budget.
Replace the SLSQP local solve with a log-barrier method (L-BFGS-B with analytic gradients, mu from 1e-2 divided by 5 over 8 stages), keeping the existing random restarts and repair.

Replace the guided restarts with a memetic phase: the first 40% of the budget is random SLSQP restarts that seed a top-8 population, and the last 60% makes Gaussian-perturbed SLSQP offspring of a random elite, with a shared per-run sigma adapted by a 1/5th-style success rule.

In the second half of the budget, half of the iterations re-optimise a random third of the best packing's circles (the largest-radius half plus a random sample of the rest) with SLSQP while the other circles stay frozen, accepting the result only if the repaired radius sum improves.
Before the free-radius SLSQP stage, run an equal-radius SLSQP stage (shared radius R maximised over the centres) and start the free-radius stage from its centres with every radius set to R.

After the random-restart loop, run a compass pattern search on the best packing's centres (random circle order, steps of +/-h in x and y, repair and accept only valid radius-sum improvements, halving h from 0.01 down to 1e-5), using the time budget up to 95% of time_limit.
Seed each non-guided SLSQP restart from a random partial packing of half the circles, mirrored by a random one of the 8 square symmetries (with small jitter), instead of uniform random centres.

issues: No sign of gaming the measurement. There is no file or network access, no pasted coordinates and no use of labels. All randomness still comes from the seeded rng.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. Guided restarts now start from 0.97 * best[1], where best[1] is the repaired, valid radii array of shape (n,). They also use a smaller perturbation sd (0.02 instead of 0.03). _repair still runs after every SLSQP call, so the final packing is still checked and shrunk if needed. The diff changes two things at once, so the result cannot be credited to either one alone.

The numbers match the provisional decision. The candidate loss is -2.937 against the incumbent's -2.9365, a difference of -0.0005 in the candidate's favour. With 1 run on each side and a noise sd of 0.0034, the sd of the difference is 0.0034*sqrt(2) ≈ 0.0048, which gives z ≈ 0.10. The harness's 0.107 most likely comes from unrounded values. This is well below any significance threshold, so rejecting is correct.

Both sides are a single run (n=1), so the comparison has very little power. The candidate's 2.937 is at the best published value (≈2.9370), but the incumbent is already at 2.9365, so that alone is not suspicious.

records.description: For guided restarts, start the radii at 0.97 times the incumbent radii and jitter the centres with scale 0.02 instead of resetting every radius to INIT_RADIUS.
Boundary-first initialisation: seed a random subset of non-guided SLSQP restarts with about 4*sqrt(n) circles placed along the four walls, the rest uniform in the interior.

After the random-restart loop, run up to 30 trust-region sequential LP steps (linprog/HiGHS) on the best repaired packing, accepting a step only if the true constraints hold and the radius sum grows, then repair and keep the result only if it beats the incumbent.
Key SLSQP ftol and iteration cap to the fraction of the budget used (1e-4/150, then 1e-6/200, then 1e-9/300 for guided restarts only in the final 20%), leaving the restart logic unchanged.

Stagnation-triggered abort of SLSQP: raise a private exception from a callback when the best feasible sum of radii stalls for 25 iterations, and return the last iterate to free time for more restarts.

After the random-restart loop, identify rattlers in the best packing, re-optimise the remaining circles with the same SLSQP model, reinsert each rattler at the largest empty spot found among 4000 random samples, repair, and keep the result only if the radius sum improves.

Initialise each non-guided SLSQP restart with Mitchell best-candidate sampling (20 seeded candidates per centre, keeping the one farthest from existing centres), leaving the guided branch, SLSQP settings and repair unchanged.
After the greedy pairwise repair, solve an LP over the radii with the centres fixed (HiGHS, all pairs, wall bounds), shrink by 1e-12 and clip, and keep whichever packing has the larger radius sum.

issues: No sign of gaming the measurement: no file or network access, no pasted coordinates, and all randomness is seeded.

LP repair is sound: all 496 pair constraints are kept, radii are bounded by wall distance, and subtracting 1e-8 per radius leaves 2e-8 of pair slack, which covers the HiGHS (~1e-9) and harness (1e-10) tolerances.

Crash risk: _valid allows zero tolerance, stricter than the harness's 1e-10. _repair output that touches exactly, with rounding error around 1e-17, is now discarded where the incumbent kept it. If every restart failed the check, solve would return None and crash. It did not happen in this run (-2.935), but a small tolerance or a fallback is advisable.
Recomputed z = -(0.0015)/(0.0034*sqrt(2)) = -0.312, against -0.300 from the harness. The gap is probably rounding and does not change the decision.
The candidate scored 0.0015 worse than the incumbent, well within one job's noise (sd 0.0034). Rejecting is consistent with the numbers.

records.description: The LP repair's HiGHS feasibility tolerance lets radii overlap by about 5e-9, so the fix shrinks LP radii by 1e-8 and accepts a candidate only if an exact overlap and wall check passes.
Scale the repaired packing outward about (0.5, 0.5) by a bisected factor t >= 1, capping radii at t*r_i, wall distance, and half the nearest-neighbour gap, and keep it only if the radius sum rises.

Replace the random-restart loop with a 4-replica ladder of SLSQP solves whose objective subtracts w times the squared overlap sum (w geometric from 1 to 100), each replica restarting from its own state plus noise, with Metropolis swaps between adjacent weights on repaired sums, returning the best repaired packing seen.
Replace the uniform random starts of half of the non-guided SLSQP restarts with a greedy largest-clearance constructive start on a 60x60 grid, using radii of 0.9 times the clearance.

Switch every remaining restart to a guided restart from the incumbent once three or more restarts have matched the best repaired sum to within 1e-4, keeping the existing time-based guided rule otherwise.

memo: Helped: only slot 1 (guided restarts in the second half, half start from the best packing), -2.9365, delta -0.0112. It is a single run and noise sd is about 0.0034, so it is unconfirmed. Not helped: nearly everything else, mostly within noise. That covers new initialisations (2, 9, 18, 29, 34), crossover (3), penalty or barrier solvers (4, 24), analytic gradients (5), gravity (10), pair pruning (11), successive halving (19), population/Metropolis schemes (20, 23), and post-polish steps (16, 28, 31, 33). Near misses, run without slot 1: 21 (-2.9396), 27 (-2.9396), 6 (-2.9386), 17 (-2.9380). Next: 1) replicate slot 1 to fix the baseline. 2) Tune the guided fraction and start time. 3) Stack slots 21/27 (the two best, same idea), then 6 and 17, one at a time on top of slot 1. 4) Final polish. Avoid more initialisation or post-polish ideas.

incumbent.description: In the second half of the time budget, half of the SLSQP restarts start from the best centres found so far with Gaussian jitter (sd 0.03), and the rest stay uniform random.

backlog.spec: After the initial random-restart phase, repeatedly take the best packing found so far, perturb the centres with Gaussian noise (sd about 0.02 to 0.05), re-run SLSQP from the perturbed state, repair, and keep the result if the radius sum improves. Use the seed-derived rng for all noise. Stop at TIME_FRACTION of the time limit.
backlog.title: Basin-hopping perturbation of best packing

backlog.spec: Reserve roughly the first 40 percent of the time budget for random restarts, then spend the remaining time doing local perturbation of the current best (small noise on centres and radii, followed by SLSQP and repair). This balances global exploration and local refinement.
backlog.title: Split time between random starts and perturbation

backlog.spec: Raise MAX_ITER from 200 to 1000 so that each SLSQP run converges fully instead of stopping early. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged. Convergence to a true local optimum typically improves the radius sum per restart.
backlog.title: Increase SLSQP iteration cap

backlog.spec: Set INIT_RADIUS to a much smaller value (about 0.01) so the starting configuration is nearly feasible and SLSQP begins with less overlap to resolve. Keep initial centre sampling as is.
backlog.title: Lower initial radius for starts

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random initial centres with a jittered 6x6 grid (32 points chosen from a 6x6 lattice with random removal of 4 points plus small uniform jitter). This spreads starts more evenly across the square, which can give better local optima than purely uniform sampling.
backlog.title: Sample initial centres from a jittered grid

backlog.spec: Instead of setting every initial radius to INIT_RADIUS, draw initial radii uniformly from [0.01, 0.1] per circle. Varied starting sizes give SLSQP more diverse starting points and can escape the symmetric configurations it otherwise tends to fall into.
backlog.title: Sample initial radii randomly

backlog.spec: Supply a Jacobian for the constraint vector and for the objective to SLSQP, computed analytically from the pairwise distance and boundary terms. Analytic gradients make each SLSQP step faster and more accurate, so more restarts fit in the time budget.
backlog.title: Analytic gradients for constraints

backlog.spec: Only include pairwise non-overlap constraints for pairs whose centres are within a cutoff (for example, distance below 2.5 times the mean radius) at the start of each SLSQP call. This shrinks the constraint vector from 496 to a few hundred entries, speeding each iteration; recompute active pairs between SLSQP calls.
backlog.title: Pair-restricted constraint set

backlog.spec: First optimise centres to maximise the minimum pairwise slack with radii fixed equal, then run SLSQP starting from that result with radii free to maximise the sum. The equal-radius stage gives a well-spread start for the free stage.
backlog.title: Two-stage optimisation with fixed radius ordering

backlog.spec: Replace the first SLSQP stage with a quadratic penalty on overlaps and boundary violations, minimised with scipy L-BFGS-B while gradually increasing the penalty weight. Then polish with SLSQP. The penalty stage is smoother and tends to find better basins before the hard constraints are enforced.
backlog.title: Penalty method with L-BFGS warm start

backlog.spec: In _repair, instead of scaling both overlapping circles by the same factor, shrink only the smaller circle of each overlapping pair, then loop. This keeps the larger circles, which contribute more to the radius sum, at their optimised size.
backlog.title: Reduce repair damage with local shrink

backlog.spec: After the repair step, run a greedy pass: for each circle in random order, grow its radius to the maximum value allowed by the boundary and its current neighbours, using the seed rng for the ordering. Repeat until no circle can grow by more than 1e-12. This recovers radius lost to the conservative repair.
backlog.title: Greedy radius inflation after repair

backlog.spec: Set SHRINK to 0 and instead rely on the repair loop's exact overlap check so that the final packing is as tight as the tolerance allows. Verify validity with a final check and fall back to the shrink margin only if the check fails.
backlog.title: Remove SHRINK safety margin

backlog.spec: Run each SLSQP restart with a small iteration budget (for example 50 iterations) first, and only continue the restarts whose intermediate radius sum is in the top quartile of those seen so far. This spends more of the budget on promising basins.
backlog.title: Early termination of poor restarts

backlog.spec: Track the distribution of final radius sums across restarts and, in the second half of the time budget, bias new restart starting points toward the neighbourhood of the best centres found (for example by mixing a random subset of best centres with new uniform points). This is a simple form of guided sampling.
backlog.title: Adaptive restart counts by time

backlog.spec: Generate initial configurations with a random symmetry (reflections and 90-degree rotations of the square) applied to a random partial packing, so starts explore symmetric families that often contain good packings for 32 circles. Use the seed rng for all draws.
backlog.title: Symmetric initialisation

backlog.spec: Move np.clip of centres inside _solve_once, before the repair step and not after, so that radii are computed from centres already inside the square. Confirm that the boundary term in _repair uses the clipped centres. This avoids boundary losses from clipping after the optimizer.
backlog.title: Remove the clip and check ordering

backlog.spec: Keep the top three packings by radius sum rather than only the best, and at the end of the time budget run one extra SLSQP polish on each. Return the best polished result. This adds a final refinement step without changing the search.
backlog.title: Dual-start selection by rank

backlog.spec: Change TIME_FRACTION so that the restart loop uses 70 percent of the budget and the final 10 percent is reserved for a polish step that re-optimises the best packing with tighter SLSQP tolerance (ftol 1e-12). Keep the harness time limit safe.
backlog.title: Lower time fraction for polish

backlog.spec: Pass options ftol=1e-12 and eps tuned for the problem to SLSQP so that the optimiser converges more tightly. Combined with MAX_ITER unchanged, this gives more accurate local optima on each restart.
backlog.title: Tighter SLSQP tolerance

backlog.spec: Given two good packings, combine them by taking circles from one in a left half-plane and from the other in the right half, cutting along a random vertical or horizontal line, then fix count to n and run SLSQP. This is a crossover operator for a small evolutionary search.
backlog.title: Random swap of circle radii between packings

backlog.spec: Maintain a population of the best eight packings. Each new start is produced by perturbing a randomly chosen member, running SLSQP, repairing, and replacing the worst member if the result is better. This keeps diversity while steadily improving.
backlog.title: Population with elitism

backlog.spec: Measure the CPU time of the first SLSQP call and set the number of restarts up front so that all of them fit within the budget with a safety margin. This avoids wasting the final partial restart and makes the time use predictable.
backlog.title: Batch of restarts sized to the budget

backlog.spec: Run SLSQP first with the objective weighting larger circles more (for example maximise the sum of r squared) and then switch to maximising the plain sum of radii. The warm-up tends to spread the big circles before the sum is maximised.
backlog.title: Radius-weighted objective warm-up

backlog.spec: Add a small penalty term to the objective that discourages very small radii, for example subtracting 1e-3 times the sum of log radii, then run the plain sum objective as a final stage. This avoids SLSQP collapsing circles to zero early.
backlog.title: Regularised objective to avoid tiny circles

backlog.spec: After repair, apply a tiny random jitter of about 1e-4 to all centres using the seed rng and rerun the repair loop, keeping the variant with the larger valid radius sum. This explores a small neighbourhood of each local optimum at negligible cost.
backlog.title: Bounded random noise during repair

backlog.spec: Instead of keeping only the single best packing, run a fixed number of restarts and return the packing with the largest radius sum among those whose radius sum is above the median of all restarts. This is a robustness tweak that reduces variance across seeds.
backlog.title: Pick restart by median not max

backlog.spec: Change INIT_LOW from 0.1 to 0.02 so initial centres can start near the boundary. Starts near the edge let SLSQP place boundary circles of larger radii earlier in the optimisation.
backlog.title: Smaller initial box margin

backlog.spec: With probability one half, seed a restart from a hexagonal-like lattice of 32 points fitted to the square, with a random rotation and scale, plus small noise, instead of uniform sampling. Dense lattice-like starts often lead to strong packings for circle problems.
backlog.title: Hexagonal-lattice seeded starts

backlog.spec: After the SLSQP and repair step produces the best packing (c, r), run up to 30 sequential linear programme steps with scipy.optimize.linprog (HiGHS). At each step, linearise every pairwise constraint d_ij - r_i - r_j >= 0 and every wall constraint around the current (c, r), and solve for displacements dc and radius changes dr that maximise sum(r + dr) inside a box trust region |dc|, |dr| <= t. Accept the step if the true nonlinear constraints are satisfied and the sum of radii increases; otherwise halve t. Stop when t < 1e-7. Apply the existing repair to the result. Only the final polish changes, so the rest of the loop is untouched.
backlog.title: Sequential LP polish of the incumbent

backlog.spec: Replace the single joint SLSQP call in _solve_once with a two-block scheme. With the centres fixed, the radii are the solution of a linear programme that maximises sum(r) subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij and r_i <= wall distance, solved with linprog. With the radii fixed, the centres are moved by a short SLSQP run that maximises the minimum slack. Alternate the two blocks for about 10 rounds or until the sum stops improving, then run the existing repair. This uses a different decomposition of the same problem and gives the radii an exact sub-solve each round.
backlog.title: Alternating block-coordinate solve: radii by LP, centres by SLSQP

backlog.spec: Add a term lam * sum_i ||c_i - (0.5, 0.5)||^2 to the SLSQP objective for each restart, with lam starting at a value of order 0.05 and decaying linearly to zero by the last SLSQP iteration. The pull toward the centre stops circles from jamming against the walls early and so reaches a wider set of basins. Because lam reaches zero, the final objective is the true sum of radii. The only change is the objective function and the lam schedule inside _solve_once.
backlog.title: Gravity annealing regulariser

backlog.spec: Inside _solve_once, tighten every pairwise and wall constraint by a clearance delta, so that d_ij >= r_i + r_j + delta and each wall constraint carries the same margin. Set delta at the start of each restart to a random value in [0.01, 0.03], and anneal it to zero over the SLSQP run by solving in three stages with delta set to 2/3, 1/3 and 0 of its starting value. Each stage starts from the previous stage's output. The aim is for intermediate packings to keep clearance so that the final unconstrained stage moves less and the repair damages less.
backlog.title: Soft clearance margin continuation

backlog.spec: With probability 0.5 per restart, optimise a point-symmetric packing first. Use n/2 free centres c_k and radii r_k, and set the remaining circles to (1 - c_k, r_k), so the packing is invariant under 180-degree rotation about (0.5, 0.5). Write the constraints in terms of the free variables, including the overlap between a circle and its own mirror image, which gives d = 2 * |c_k - 0.5| >= 2 r_k. Solve this half-size problem with SLSQP, which has about a quarter of the constraints, then use its output as the start for a full unconstrained SLSQP run on all n circles, followed by repair. This explores symmetric basins that the full problem rarely reaches.
backlog.title: Central-symmetry reduced-variable stage

backlog.spec: For each restart, solve for n + 2 circles instead of n, with the two extra circles starting at random positions and the same initial radius. After SLSQP and repair, delete the two smallest-radius circles, which can be found by sorting the radii, and run a second short SLSQP on the remaining n circles starting from the pruned configuration. Then repair and keep the best packing as before. The extra circles give the optimiser slack to rearrange jammed regions, and removing the smallest circles afterward is a cheap way to lose little. Keep the total time limit and the best-of-restarts logic unchanged.
backlog.title: Over-provisioned solve with pruning

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed guided probability in solve with an upper-confidence-bound bandit over two arms, a fresh random start and a guided start from the incumbent. For each arm, track the number of pulls and the mean improvement in the sum of radii over the incumbent, where improvement is zero when the restart does not beat the incumbent. At each restart, choose the arm with the highest mean plus sqrt(2 ln(T) / pulls), with a constraint that each arm is pulled at least twice first. This replaces the time-based switch at half budget, so guidance starts as soon as it proves useful and stops if it does not. Use the seed argument for all randomness.
backlog.title: UCB bandit over restart modes

backlog.spec: Keep the best K = 3 distinct packings found during the random-restart phase, ranked by the sum of radii after repair. Reserve the last 15 percent of the CPU time budget for these: give each of the K packings a single SLSQP run with MAX_ITER raised to 1000 and a tight ftol of 1e-12, starting from its own best configuration, then repair each result. Return whichever has the largest sum of radii. This spends a little extra time on the best candidates, where longer convergence is more likely to matter than on new random starts.
backlog.title: Top-K long final SLSQP

backlog.spec: When a guided restart is chosen, do not start from the incumbent's coordinates directly. Instead pick one of the eight symmetries of the unit square at random, using the seeded rng: identity, the three rotations, and the four reflections. Apply it to the incumbent centres, c -> T(c), with T mapping [0,1]^2 to itself, and keep the radii unchanged. Then add the existing Gaussian jitter and run SLSQP as before. Under the square's symmetry group this gives a different starting point with the same packing quality, so the guided restarts explore different neighbours of the same basin.
backlog.title: Square-symmetry transform of the incumbent for guided starts

backlog.spec: After repair, run a local search on the best packing. Pick a random circle, remove it, and find the point in the square that allows the largest radius for it given the other circles, using a grid search over candidate points followed by a local Nelder-Mead refinement, which makes the candidate radius equal to the minimum of the clearance to the walls and to the other circles. If the new total sum of radii, after re-optimising the other radii with a short SLSQP on fixed centres, is higher than the old sum, keep the move. Repeat for about 40 random circles or until the time slice runs out. This is a deterministic, hole-targeted move that differs from random jitter.
backlog.title: Cyclic relocation sweep on the incumbent

backlog.spec: Each guided restart builds its start by growth rather than from uniform random centres. Keep a cache of the best packing found for n-1 circles, obtained by running the same routine on n-1 with a shorter budget at the start of solve (about 15% of the time). For each guided restart, take that packing, add one circle at the point farthest from all existing circles and walls (sampled on a 200x200 grid), set its radius to 0.01, and run SLSQP from there. Then continue with the usual repair and selection. The best n-1 packing is only a seed, so the n circle result still comes from SLSQP on n circles.
backlog.title: Incremental insertion from the best n-1 packing

backlog.spec: After the first half of the budget, perturb the incumbent by a destroy-and-repair move instead of a global jitter. Pick a random centre point and radius R uniformly in [0.2, 0.4]. Remove every circle whose centre lies within R of that point and re-place the same number of circles uniformly in that disc, with radii 0.01. Run SLSQP on all n circles from this start with a small iteration cap, then repair and keep the result only if its radius sum is larger than the incumbent's. Use the seed rng for all draws. This is a local move that keeps most of the packing intact, unlike a global perturbation.
backlog.title: Large-neighbourhood destroy and repair in a random disc

backlog.spec: Replace SLSQP in _solve_once with a barrier method. Variables are centres and radii. The objective is minus the sum of radii plus mu times minus the sum of log of every constraint slack (pairwise distance minus radius sum, wall clearances, and radii). Minimise with scipy L-BFGS-B using analytic gradients, starting with mu=1e-2 and dividing mu by 5 after each solve, for about 8 stages. Infeasible starts are handled by taking the first stage with the clipped centres and a tiny radius. After the final stage, pass the result through the existing repair. This is a different solver family from SLSQP and may reach more basins per second.
backlog.title: Log-barrier interior-point solve in place of SLSQP

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, run a least-squares stage with scipy.optimize.least_squares (method 'lm' or 'trf') on residuals. The residuals are max(0, r_i + r_j - d_ij) for each pair, max(0, r_i - x_i) and the other three wall residuals, and a small weight times (-r_i) so the radii grow. Use the same random start as SLSQP. Run for at most 100 function evaluations, then hand the result to the existing SLSQP stage to remove residual overlaps and to optimise the sum exactly. The least-squares stage uses a different algorithm from the earlier quadratic penalty, which was rejected.
backlog.title: Levenberg-Marquardt penalty stage before SLSQP

backlog.spec: Add a continuation on the constraint form in SLSQP. In the first stage, replace the hard pairwise and wall constraints with one smooth objective: maximise sum of radii minus (1/beta) times log-sum-exp over all clearances, where clearance is distance minus radius sum for pairs and wall distance minus radius for walls. Use beta = 20, then 80, then 320, each solved with L-BFGS-B using analytic gradients. Finish with the existing SLSQP hard-constraint solve from the result. Beta raises the sharpness of the clearance minimum, so the interior of the feasible set is explored before the constraints become hard.
backlog.title: Soft-min clearance continuation with log-sum-exp

backlog.spec: Rescale the decision variables before calling SLSQP. Let centres be x = 0.5 + u times something, but keep the structure simple: define the variables as u = centre and s = 10 times radius, so that radii near 0.1 are of order 1, close to the scale of the centres. Write the objective and constraints in terms of (u, s) and divide each constraint by 10 when its scale is radius-based. Map back to centres and radii before repair. Use the same restarts and budget. The aim is to stop SLSQP from making poor steps where the radii and centre coordinates have very different scales, which may reduce wasted iterations at n=32.
backlog.title: Variable scaling for SLSQP conditioning

backlog.spec: Add a radius-continuation restart type to the non-guided restarts. Pick a target rho by bisection between 0.05 and 0.2. For a fixed rho, all radii are set to rho and SLSQP maximises the minimum clearance s over centres (constraints: distance minus 2 rho is at least s, wall clearance is at least rho). If the optimum s is at least 0 keep the rho as feasible and raise it, otherwise lower it. About 6 bisection steps. Use the feasible centres as the start for the usual sum-of-radii SLSQP, with radii initialised to the feasible common rho. This is a different start schedule that enforces feasibility first, then grows the radius sum.
backlog.title: Feasibility bisection on a common radius

backlog.spec: Track the radius sums and centre sets of every local optimum found so far. After each SLSQP restart, compare the result with the stored optima using the sorted radius vector and the centre set up to permutation. If the result matches a stored optimum (sorted radii within 1e-4 in every component), count it as a repeat and do not spend extra time on it. Restart with a fresh random start whenever a repeat occurs, up to 3 repeats in a row, and then keep the best result as before. The aim is to use the time budget on new basins rather than revisiting the same packings.
backlog.title: Tabu rejection of already-seen local optima

backlog.spec: After the search phase, take the incumbent and run SLSQP again from its own output with maxiter 300 and ftol 1e-12. Repeat this warm restart while the radius sum improves by more than 1e-9, up to 10 rounds. Each round starts from the previous round's centres and radii with no noise. Apply repair after the final round. Reserve the last 10% of the time budget for this loop, so that the search phase uses only 70% of the budget. The change targets the final few thousandths of the radius sum, which random restarts do not reach.
backlog.title: Iterated warm-restart polish of the incumbent

backlog.spec: At the start of each guided restart, apply a short stochastic relaxation to the incumbent before SLSQP. For 200 steps, pick a random circle, move its centre by a Gaussian with sd 0.01 scaled by its radius, and accept the move if no pairwise overlap or wall violation is created when the radius is kept equal to the current value. If rejected, keep the old position. Then run the usual SLSQP from the relaxed centres. This is a Monte Carlo move that can slide circles past each other to escape jammed configurations, and it is a different perturbation type from Gaussian jitter of all centres.
backlog.title: Stochastic boundary-contact relaxation of the incumbent

backlog.spec: After the best packing is chosen, identify the active contacts: pairs with gap below 1e-7 and circle-wall contacts with slack below 1e-7. Build the system of equalities for these active constraints (pair distance equals sum of radii, wall distance equals radius) and solve it with Newton's method, using the least-squares step (numpy.linalg.lstsq) because the system is usually over- or under-determined. Accept a step only if the sum of radii increases and the full constraint check still passes in double precision. Repeat for at most 20 iterations, then run the existing repair. This is a cheap exact polish that the SLSQP tolerance leaves out.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton polish of the final packing

backlog.spec: Keep the existing random-restart and guided loop, but after it finishes, take the top 3 distinct repaired packings and polish each with scipy.optimize.minimize using method='trust-constr'. Pass the same objective (minus the sum of radii) and the same inequality constraints as a NonlinearConstraint with finite-difference Jacobian, or with a sparse analytic Jacobian of the pair and wall constraints. Give each polish a fixed share of the remaining time (about 10 percent of the budget each). Keep the packing with the largest valid sum after repair. Use only the seed rng for any randomness.
backlog.title: trust-constr final polish of the top candidates

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random initial centres of a fraction of the non-guided restarts with a constructive start. Place circles one at a time: on a 60 by 60 grid over [0,1]^2, find the grid point whose distance to the nearest placed centre and to the walls is largest, with a small random tie-break from the seed rng; put the next circle there with initial radius equal to that clearance times 0.9. Use the resulting centres and radii as the SLSQP starting point. Keep the rest of the restart loop unchanged. The goal is structured starts that are not lattices and not uniform noise.
backlog.title: Greedy largest-hole constructive start

backlog.spec: Maintain a small population (about 8) of packings. Each generation, make offspring by perturbing an elite packing with Gaussian noise whose per-circle scale is adapted from the success rate of recent offspring (a simple 1/5th-style rule), then run the existing SLSQP local solve on each offspring and repair it. Keep the best 8 by valid radius sum as the next population. Seed the initial population from the random restarts already in the code. Share the time budget so that the population phase uses the last 60 percent of the time. Only numpy and the existing functions are used.
backlog.title: Memetic search: CMA-style population over centres with SLSQP local search

backlog.spec: Start with a pool of 16 random initial configurations. Run each for 40 SLSQP iterations, rank by sum of radii after repair, and keep the top half. Continue the survivors from their current state for another 40 iterations, again keep the top half, and repeat with doubling iteration budgets until one candidate remains. Then start a new pool and repeat while time remains. Keep the best valid packing found across all pools. Budget each pool so that the whole procedure stops at TIME_FRACTION of the time limit, measured with time.process_time().
backlog.title: Successive halving over a pool of short SLSQP runs

backlog.spec: Optimise s_i with r_i = s_i squared, so that the non-negativity of radii is enforced by construction and the radius constraint r >= 0 is removed from the SLSQP constraint vector. The wall constraints become c minus s squared, and the pair constraints use s squared for both circles. Initialise s as sqrt of INIT_RADIUS. Convert back to radii r = s squared before the repair step. Everything else (restart loop, guidance, time limit) stays the same. This changes the conditioning of the radius variables and the active set near zero radius.
backlog.title: Squared-radius reparametrisation

backlog.spec: Impose a minimum radius r_min on every circle inside SLSQP, and ramp r_min over the run: start at 0 for the first 30 percent of the time budget, then increase it linearly to 0.5 times the mean radius of the current best packing by the end of the budget. Enforce it as an extra inequality constraint r_i minus r_min at least zero. Before each restart's SLSQP call, set r_min from the current elapsed fraction. This pushes the search away from degenerate configurations with a few tiny circles and steers restarts toward uniform-looking packings, while keeping the final repair unchanged.
backlog.title: Radius lower-bound homotopy

backlog.spec: Take the best packing and pick a random subset of about one third of the circles, chosen as the k circles with the largest radii plus a random subset of the rest. Re-run SLSQP on the full set but with the circles outside the subset frozen (their centres and radii treated as constants and removed from the variable vector, with their constraints against the subset kept). Alternate random subset choices for the remaining time, accepting a new packing only if its repaired radius sum is larger. This is a block-coordinate search that works at the level of groups of circles rather than single moves.
backlog.title: Hierarchical subset re-optimisation of the incumbent

backlog.spec: Run a single chain instead of independent restarts. The current state is a repaired packing. Each step, perturb it by re-initialising a random 3 to 5 circles uniformly in the square and running SLSQP from the perturbed packing, then repair. Accept the new packing if its radius sum is larger, otherwise accept with probability exp((new minus current) divided by T), where T decays geometrically from 0.01 to 0.0001 over the time budget. Keep the best packing seen. Draw all randomness from the seed rng. This uses an annealed acceptance rule rather than the fixed guided rule.
backlog.title: Metropolis-accepted chain of local optima

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform draw of initial centres in the non-guided restarts with points from a scrambled Halton sequence in bases 2 and 3 over [0.05, 0.95] squared, with the digit scrambling permutation and the starting index drawn from the seed rng. Each restart takes the next block of n points from the sequence, so successive restarts cover the square more evenly than independent uniform draws. Keep the radii initialisation and the rest of the loop unchanged.
backlog.title: Scrambled Halton starts for the restart centres

backlog.spec: For a non-guided restart, draw initial centres one at a time with Mitchell's best-candidate rule: for each new centre, generate about 20 uniform candidates in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2 from the seeded rng, and keep the candidate farthest from all centres placed so far. This gives well-spread starts with no lattice structure. Leave the guided branch, SLSQP settings, and repair unchanged.
backlog.title: Best-candidate (Mitchell) centre sampling

backlog.spec: After sampling the initial centres for a non-guided restart, compute each centre's approximate Voronoi cell area by Monte Carlo (about 4000 uniform points in the square from the seeded rng, assigned to nearest centre). Set the initial radius of circle i to a constant times sqrt(area_i / pi), with the constant chosen so the mean initial radius is INIT_RADIUS. The SLSQP start then reflects the local free space instead of a uniform 0.05. Nothing else changes.
backlog.title: Voronoi-cell-proportional initial radii

backlog.spec: Add a second initialiser for about a third of the non-guided restarts. Start with n points at random positions, with zero radii and random velocities from the seeded rng. Run a short event-free soft-disk simulation: at each step, grow all radii by a small rate, push overlapping pairs apart by an elastic force proportional to overlap, and reflect velocities at the walls, for about 300 steps. Stop growing a circle once it touches a neighbour or wall. Pass the resulting centres and radii to SLSQP as the start. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged.
backlog.title: Lubachevsky-Stillinger style growth initialiser

backlog.spec: On the incumbent after repair, identify rattlers: circles with no contact, meaning slack above 1e-6 to every other circle and every wall. Remove them, re-optimise the remaining circles with the same SLSQP model for a fixed number of iterations, then reinsert each rattler at the centre of the largest empty region found by sampling 4000 random points and maximising the distance to existing circles and walls, with its radius set to that clearance. Run the repair again and keep the result only if its sum of radii improves.
backlog.title: Rattler removal and reinsertion polish

backlog.spec: Pass a callback to the SLSQP minimize call that records the objective and the maximum constraint violation at each iteration. If the best feasible sum of radii has not improved by more than 1e-5 over the last 25 iterations, raise a private exception that the solver wrapper catches, and return the last iterate. This frees time for more restarts, since most poor restarts plateau well before MAX_ITER. Keep the restart and guided logic unchanged.
backlog.title: Stagnation-triggered abort of SLSQP

backlog.spec: Run a fixed ladder of 4 replicas per solve, each with a different weight w in a geometric ladder from 1 to 100 on an overlap penalty term added to the SLSQP objective (sum of radii minus w times the squared overlap sum). Each replica is a local optimiser starting from the current incumbent plus noise. After each sweep, propose swaps between adjacent weights using the Metropolis rule on the repaired sums, using the seeded rng. Return the best repaired packing seen across all replicas and sweeps.
backlog.title: Replica exchange over overlap-penalty weights

backlog.spec: Replace the SLSQP objective with the sum of min(r_i, cap), where cap starts at 0.5 and is raised over three stages to 1.0 (the bounds stay as they are). Each stage warm-starts from the previous one. At the final stage the objective is the usual sum of radii, so the last stage recovers the original problem. The cap discourages one large circle from absorbing free space early, which may help the search settle on balanced packings.
backlog.title: Annealed radius cap in the objective

backlog.spec: For about a third of the non-guided restarts, split n into four groups of roughly n/4 (by random assignment from the seeded rng). Solve each group independently as a packing in its own quadrant of the unit square (quadrant side 0.5 with the same SLSQP model), then rescale the four solutions into the full square with their centres and radii halved. Feed the merged packing to one global SLSQP stage as the start, then repair as usual. This tests whether recursive structure helps the search reach the good configurations.
backlog.title: Divide-and-conquer quadrant packing

backlog.spec: Instead of the fixed MAX_ITER=200 for every restart, draw each restart's iteration cap from a log-uniform distribution on [60, 800] using the seeded rng, and pass it as the maxiter option. Short caps give cheap diverse starts and long caps let some restarts converge fully. Keep the guided rule and the repair unchanged. The expected time per restart stays about the same because the time check remains as before.
backlog.title: Log-uniform random SLSQP iteration cap per restart

backlog.spec: After _repair, scale all centres about (0.5, 0.5) by a factor t >= 1 found by bisection, and set radii to min(r_i * t, distance-to-wall for the new centre, and half of the nearest-neighbour gap). Keep the largest t whose resulting radii give a valid packing under the exact pairwise check, then keep the packing only if its radius sum increases. Apply this to the best packing once at the end of solve and to each candidate before comparison. The step is feasibility-preserving by construction, so the harness check stays safe.
backlog.title: Global expansion of the repaired packing

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, replace the linear objective -sum(r) with -sum(r**p), where p is annealed from 0.5 to 1.0 over the SLSQP stages of each restart (two stages: p=0.5 then p=1.0). The concave-to-linear path favours configurations where many radii grow together and reduces early lock-in onto unequal local optima. Keep the constraints unchanged. Only the final stage with p=1 is used for ranking, so the reported quantity is still the sum of radii.
backlog.title: Power-mean objective annealing

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random initial centres of a fraction (say half) of non-guided restarts with a configuration obtained by minimising the Riesz energy sum over pairs of 1/||c_i - c_j||^s plus a wall term that keeps centres in [0.05, 0.95]^2. Draw the exponent s uniformly from [1, 8] using the seed rng, run 100 L-BFGS-B iterations with numeric or analytic gradient from a random start, then pass the result to the existing SLSQP stage with initial radius INIT_RADIUS. This gives well-spread starts without any explicit circle layout.
backlog.title: Riesz-energy initial configuration

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, run a first SLSQP stage with a single shared radius variable R for all circles (variables: 2n centres plus R, maximise R subject to the same pairwise and wall constraints with r_i = R). Use the resulting centres as the start of the existing free-radius stage, with radii initialised to the equal radius R. This coarse-to-fine step starts the free-radius problem from a feasible, evenly spread configuration rather than from random radii.
backlog.title: Equal-radius pre-stage before free radii

backlog.spec: For a random subset of non-guided restarts, place about 4*sqrt(n) circles along the four edges of the square at random positions inside the wall margin (positions chosen from the seed rng with spacing jittered), then place the remaining circles uniformly in the interior. Pass the combined centres to the existing SLSQP stage. Boundary circles are known to be pushed to walls in good packings, so this biases the start toward the correct contact structure.
backlog.title: Boundary-first initialisation

backlog.spec: Inside _solve_once, run the SLSQP solve in k=3 sequential stages. At each stage, include the non-overlap constraint only for a random 60 percent of pairs (chosen with the seed rng), plus all pairs whose centres were within 2.5 times the mean radius at the stage start. After each stage, recompute the full pair set and check the violation. Keep the last full-constraint stage as the output. This reduces the constraint count per SLSQP step and lets the solver explore more configurations per unit of CPU time.
backlog.title: Stochastic pair-subset resampling per stage

backlog.spec: For guided restarts, initialise the radii from the incumbent radii multiplied by 0.97 and the centres from the incumbent plus Gaussian jitter of scale 0.02, instead of resetting all radii to INIT_RADIUS. Lowering the radii keeps the start close to feasibility and lets SLSQP reach a nearby better optimum in fewer iterations. Keep the rest of the guided logic unchanged.
backlog.title: Warm start from shrunken incumbent radii

backlog.spec: After the random-restart loop, take the best packing and run a compass pattern search over the centre coordinates: for each circle in random order, try moving its centre by plus or minus a step h in x and in y, re-run _repair on the modified packing, and accept the move if the radius sum improves. Halve h after a full sweep with no improvement, starting at h=0.01 and stopping at h=1e-5. Use the seed rng for ordering. This derivative-free refinement does not rely on SLSQP convergence and can escape its stationary points.
backlog.title: Coordinate pattern search on the incumbent

backlog.spec: After a packing is found, compute for each circle the largest radius it could hold at its current centre given the other centres and walls (the minimum of the wall distances and half the nearest-neighbour gap). Sort circles by this free-space value and assign the radii in sorted order, largest radius to the largest free space, using the repair routine on the reassigned radii. Then run a short SLSQP on radii only with the centres fixed to re-optimise sizes. Keep the reassigned packing only if its radius sum is larger.
backlog.title: Size assignment by free-space matching

backlog.spec: For each candidate packing, alternate two steps for a fixed small number of rounds: (a) with centres fixed, maximise sum of radii as a linear program over the radii subject to the linearised pairwise constraints r_i + r_j <= d_ij and wall constraints r_i <= wall distance, using scipy.optimize.linprog with the highs method; (b) with radii fixed at the LP solution, run a few SLSQP iterations on the centres only. Stop when the sum changes by less than 1e-9. Finish with the repair routine. The LP step gives exact radii for fixed centres, which the joint SLSQP may not reach.
backlog.title: Alternating radius LP and centre SLSQP

backlog.spec: After each repair in the restart loop, take the incumbent (or the current candidate) and remove the circle with the smallest radius. Find the largest empty region by sampling about 2000 seeded random points and taking the one with the greatest distance to all remaining centres and walls. Place the removed circle there with radius 0, then run one SLSQP solve from that start with MAX_ITER and the usual constraints. Keep the result only if its repaired sum of radii beats the incumbent. This is a single, self-contained move, separate from the zero-contact rattler reinsertion idea.
backlog.title: Relocate the smallest circle into the largest hole

backlog.spec: After an SLSQP solve, estimate the constraint multipliers by solving a non-negative least-squares problem: the gradient of the objective should match a non-negative combination of the gradients of the near-active constraints (contacts within 1e-4). Keep only the constraints with a positive multiplier. Re-run SLSQP once, on this active set plus a slack margin of 1e-3 on the other pairs, and then re-check all pairs in the repair step. Use the same seeds and time budget. This targets the constraint structure rather than the starting points.
backlog.title: Lagrange-multiplier reweighting of the constraint set

backlog.spec: For a random subset of restarts (for example 30 percent), impose mirror symmetry about the vertical line x = 0.5. Use m = n//2 free centres and their mirror images, plus one centre on the axis when n is odd. Build the full centre array from the free variables and the radii as free variables, and run SLSQP on this reduced vector with the same constraints evaluated on the full set. Then unfold, run one unconstrained SLSQP polish on all 2n+n variables, and repair. This is distinct from the existing central-symmetry stage, because it uses a reflection instead of a point reflection.
backlog.title: Reflection-symmetric reduced-variable stage

backlog.spec: For a restart, pick a random aspect ratio a from [0.85, 1.15]. Solve the SLSQP packing in the rectangle [0, a] x [0, 1] with its own wall constraints, starting from a uniform random layout, with a and the walls as fixed parameters. Then rescale the centres to x times 1/a so that they fit the unit square. Use the rescaled centres as the start for a second SLSQP solve in the unit square, with the usual INIT_RADIUS. This gives structured starts from different geometries while keeping every initial state inside the square.
backlog.title: Stretched-box warm start

backlog.spec: Replace the greedy pairwise repair with a single LP. Keep the centres fixed. Solve a linprog problem that maximises the sum of radii subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij for every pair with d_ij below 2 times the largest radius, r_i <= wall distance for each circle, and r_i >= 0, using the HiGHS method. Round the solution down by 1e-12 and then clip. Compare the resulting sum with the current greedy repair and keep the larger of the two. This repair is fully feasible by construction and loses less radius than uniform pairwise shrinking.
backlog.title: Linear-programming repair in place of pairwise shrinking

backlog.spec: Pass ftol and the iteration cap to SLSQP through a schedule keyed to elapsed time. In the first 40 percent of the budget, use ftol 1e-4 and MAX_ITER 150, which is cheap. In the next 40 percent, use ftol 1e-6 with MAX_ITER 200. In the last 20 percent, use ftol 1e-9 and MAX_ITER 300, applied only to the current best candidate. Do not change the restart logic. The goal is to spend early time on breadth and the final time on exact convergence of the best packing.
backlog.title: Coarse-to-fine SLSQP tolerance schedule

backlog.spec: Add a penalty term lam times the sum of (r_i minus mean r)^2 to the SLSQP objective, with lam set per restart to a random value in [0, 0.05]. Draw lam for each restart from the seed rng. Solve with the penalty included, then run a final SLSQP solve without it, starting from the penalised solution and using the usual constraints. Repair and keep the result as normal. This regularisation pushes radii toward a more uniform distribution first, then lets the true objective decide the final sizes.
backlog.title: Soft radius-variance penalty annealed to zero

backlog.spec: Track the repaired sum of radii for each restart. When the best value has been matched to within 1e-4 by at least three independent restarts, treat the random-start phase as converged. From that point, every restart is a guided restart drawn from the incumbent, using the jitter scale already in use, and the loop continues until the time budget is spent. Otherwise keep the current logic unchanged. This replaces the fixed time-based switch with one driven by agreement among restarts.
backlog.title: Convergence-triggered switch to guided restarts

backlog.spec: For a random subset of non-guided restarts, seed the centres on concentric rings. Choose a random number of rings k in {2, 3}. Place the rings at distances from the walls that are spaced evenly, with the outer ring just inside the square. Distribute the n circles across the rings in proportion to each ring's circumference, with a seeded random phase and a small jitter. Set the initial radii to INIT_RADIUS and run the normal SLSQP. This mimics the ring-like structure that large packings often show near the boundary, and it is distinct from the hexagonal and symmetric seeds already tried.
backlog.title: Concentric-ring initialisation near the walls

backlog.spec: For a fraction of restarts, assign each circle to one of k = 3 size classes, with k drawn from {2, 3} and class sizes set by a seeded random split of n. Solve SLSQP in which circles in the same class share a common radius variable, so the radius vector has k entries. This is a small, low-dimensional problem and converges quickly. Then release the class constraints by giving each circle its own radius, starting from the class radii, and run a final SLSQP solve with the usual constraints. Repair and keep the best result. This is a size-class homotopy and it is not the single equal-radius stage already tried.
backlog.title: Size-class homotopy with k discrete radius classes

backlog.spec: For a random half of the non-guided restarts, set the initial radii to 0.12 instead of INIT_RADIUS=0.05, keeping the uniform random centres. SLSQP starts with heavy overlaps and must resolve them, which may land in different basins than the usual feasible-ish start. Keep the rest of the pipeline (clip, repair, best-of selection) unchanged. The seed rng decides which restarts are inflated.
backlog.title: Over-inflated overlapping starts

backlog.spec: For a random subset of non-guided restarts, place the n centres on a Vogel spiral: point k at radius sqrt((k+0.5)/n) times 0.45 from the box centre (0.5, 0.5), angle k times the golden angle plus a random phase drawn from rng. Add Gaussian jitter of 0.02 and clip into [0.05, 0.95]. Then run the same SLSQP, repair and selection. This is a different low-discrepancy radial pattern from Halton, Mitchell or grid starts.
backlog.title: Sunflower (Vogel spiral) initial configuration

backlog.spec: After the random-restart loop, take the incumbent and pick k uniformly from {2,...,5} from rng. Remove the k circles with the smallest radii and reinsert each one at the point, out of 3000 uniform random candidates in [0,1]^2, that maximises the distance to all remaining centres minus their radii (the largest free space). Set the reinserted radii to 0.01, then run SLSQP from this start and keep the result if its repaired sum of radii is larger. Repeat for as long as the time budget allows. This moves whole sets of small circles, not one at a time.
backlog.title: Ruin-and-recreate on k random small circles

backlog.spec: Each non-guided SLSQP restart draws positive weights w_i from U(0.6, 1.4) with the seed rng and maximises sum(w_i * r_i) instead of the plain sum of radii. The weights stay fixed for the whole solve. Repair and selection still score the true, unweighted sum of radii, so only the search path changes. Guided restarts keep the unweighted objective. This is a persistent weighting that diversifies basins, not a warm-up.
backlog.title: Random per-restart objective weights

backlog.spec: Replace the radius variables r with s = log(r) in the SLSQP decision vector, so r = exp(s) and positivity holds automatically. Keep the objective as the negative sum of exp(s) and the same constraints, with r_i replaced by exp(s_i) in the non-overlap and wall constraints. Initialise s at log(INIT_RADIUS). Post-process with the existing clip and repair. This changes the conditioning of small-radius directions and has no extra hyperparameters.
backlog.title: Log-radius parametrisation

backlog.spec: Inside _solve_once, first run SLSQP with only the non-overlap constraints for pairs whose start centres are within 2.5 times the start radius sum, plus all wall constraints. After each solve, compute all pairwise violations of the returned packing. If any pair with distance less than r_i + r_j minus 1e-6 is missing from the set, add those pairs and re-solve from the last iterate. Stop after 5 rounds or when none are violated. This is exact at convergence, unlike a fixed pair subset, which failed earlier because it used the starting centres only.
backlog.title: Lazy pairwise constraint generation

backlog.spec: For each restart with probability 0.5, first solve a coarse problem with m = floor(n/2) composite circles. Each composite is at the mass-weighted centroid of its two nearest-neighbour circles, with radius sqrt(r_a^2 + r_b^2) capped by the wall distance. Solve that m-circle problem with the same SLSQP, then split each composite back into its two members, placed at the composite centre plus or minus 0.5 times its radius along a random direction from rng. Solve the full n-circle problem from this start with SLSQP, then repair. This is a bold multiscale start that may find better global structure.
backlog.title: Coarse-to-fine multiscale solve

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed guided/non-guided split with a Beta-Bernoulli bandit over three start families: uniform random, sunflower spiral, and over-inflated overlapping starts. Each arm starts with Beta(1,1). After each restart, an arm succeeds if its repaired sum of radii beats the incumbent. Choose the arm for each restart by sampling each Beta posterior with rng and taking the largest sample. Keep the guided option from the incumbent in the second half of the budget unchanged. This adapts the initialisation mix within a single run.
backlog.title: Thompson sampling over initialisation families

backlog.spec: For each restart, after the first SLSQP solve, multiply all radii by a factor 0.9 with centres fixed and re-solve SLSQP with the radii as variables starting from these shrunken values. Then repeat the shrink-and-solve step once more with factor 0.97. The homotopy moves the optimiser through a sequence of slightly feasible states and lets circles reorganise before the final free-radius solve. Repair and selection are unchanged. This is a schedule over the solve, not an initialisation.
backlog.title: Shrink-then-regrow radius homotopy

backlog.spec: In the second half of the budget, for guided restarts, rotate the incumbent centres about (0.5, 0.5) by a random angle drawn from rng, uniform in [0, 2 pi), and apply a random reflection with probability 0.5 before adding the existing jitter. Clip the centres into the box and radii are reset to 0.9 times the incumbent radii. Only this guided start changes, so the rotated packing is a fresh basin to refine. The random square symmetries are the only new variable.
backlog.title: Random orientation of the subproblem around the incumbent
